This appeal has been preferred by appellant/driver under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is arising out of the order dated 23.02.2018 passed by the First Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sendhwa, District - Barwani (MP) in Claim Case No.105 of 2017 on account of Sant Kumar vs Malik Shaikh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24243897/

sentences.text: (2) The brief facts of the case is that the respondent No.1 filed a claim case against the appellant and respondent No.2 alleging that on 25.01.2013, when the respondent No.1 was going with respondent No.4 on a motorcycle bearing registration no. MP46MB-8523 and when they reached Gram Vasavi Sendhwa Palsud Road at that time the appellant who was driving the motorcycle and on that incident, the respondent No.1 was injured on the spot.
(3) Thereafter, the respondent No.1 has filed the claim petition against the driver, owner and the Insurance Company.

(4) The appellant filed written statement and denied all the averments made in the claim petition and further submitted that at the time of incident the offending vehicle was not driven by appellant and the respondent No.1 was falsely implicated the offending vehicle in the claim case.

(5) The learned claims tribunal after recording the evidence has found that at the time of incident the appellant was driving the offending vehicle and therefore the learned claims Tribunal has given the right of recovery to the respondent No.1 against the appellant.

(6) The Tribunal has framed the issues and on the basis of pleadings of both the parties and after hearing both of them has allowed the claim case and has awarded the compensation of Rs.44,000/-
against the appellant and other persons.

(7) The appellant has filed the appeal on the ground that he was falsely implicated in the aforesaid case and he was not driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident and the learned Tribunal has committed grave error in not properly considering the document Ex.D/1 and inspite of this the learned Tribunal has fastened the liability upon the appellant.
(7) I have heard counsel for both the parties and have perused the entire record of the case file with due care.

(8) After hearing counsel for both the parties, it was found that the police has registered the case against the appellant/driver and after due investigation, chargesheet has been filed before the Tribunal and the claimant has filed the criminal record and has adduced the evidence.
The appellant has also filed the criminal record.
Ex. D/8 shows that he was convicted under Section 279 and 337 of IPC by concerned Magistrate in the aforesaid case registered against him.
(9) So considering the evidence adduced before Tribunal, it was found that the claims Tribunal has not committed any error in holding the fact that the appellant was responsible for the accident.
(10) With the aforesaid facts and in the considered opinion of this Court, this appeal is devoid of any substance and is dismissed accordingly.
